issues.t: CUE touchscreen cracks, freezes or stops responding
issues.sym: The center touchscreen develops a cracked or bubbled look, presses register in the wrong place or not at all, the screen freezes, or it shuts off at random. Radio, navigation and some settings can become hard to use.
issues.why: The CUE screen has a touch layer that can separate (delaminate) and crack with age and heat. Some screens also lock up or reboot from software or module faults.
issues.next: This does not affect how the car drives, but it can block climate and phone functions. Ask a dealer or an audio shop whether only the touch layer needs replacing instead of a whole new unit.

issues.t: Rear end sags or drops (leveling system)
issues.sym: The rear of the car sits low, often after being parked overnight, or drops while driving. The ride may turn harsh and bumpy.
issues.why: The rear self-leveling system uses air-assisted shocks and a small compressor. Air leaks, a worn compressor or a faulty height sensor let the rear settle. GM issued bulletins for rear sag after the car sits.
issues.next: Avoid heavy loads and towing until it is fixed. Have the leveling system checked for air leaks, compressor function and sensor faults.

issues.t: Rear shock absorbers leak or crack
issues.sym: Oily residue on the rear shocks, a bouncy or harsh ride, or knocking over bumps.
issues.why: The rear shocks can leak fluid or crack. GM has a bulletin on shock and strut leaks.
issues.next: Have the shocks inspected. Leaking shocks reduce control on rough roads and can cause the rear to sag.

issues.t: Transmission shudder or harsh, slipping shifts
issues.sym: A shudder when pulling away or shifting, harsh 2-3 or 3-2 shifts, slips or flares in rpm, or the transmission not shifting properly.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic can develop valve body wear and adapt poorly. GM issued bulletins that replace the valve body housings for shudder and harsh shifts, and others to reset shift learning.
issues.next: Note when it happens and ask a dealer to check for the valve body and shift-adapt bulletins. Do not wait if it slips, since slipping wears the clutches.

issues.t: Transmission cooler lines leak
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the front of the car or a burning smell after driving.
issues.why: The lines that carry fluid to the transmission cooler can leak at their joints.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and do not drive far if it is low. Replace the leaking line.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or growl
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and over time.
issues.why: The wheel hub bearings wear out. Owners report both front and rear bearing replacements.
issues.next: Have the hubs checked for play. A worn bearing can overheat or fail, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Sunroof binds, makes noise or leaks
issues.sym: The sunroof moves in jerks, reverses on its own, makes noise, the sunshade fails, or water drips inside. One owner reported the glass failing on its own.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for sunroof binding, noise, auto-reverse and water leaks, often from the track and drain parts.
issues.next: Keep the sunroof closed and the drains clear. Have it checked before water damages the headliner or wiring.

issues.t: Battery drains and car will not start
issues.sym: The battery goes flat after the car sits, sometimes within a short time.
issues.why: Owners report battery drains on early cars. A module that stays awake or a weak battery are common causes.
issues.next: Have a shop test the battery and run a parasitic draw test to find what stays on.

issues.t: Battery drain from the memory seat module
issues.sym: Repeated dead batteries after the car sits overnight or for a few days.
issues.why: GM found the memory seat module can wake the car network and keep it from sleeping, draining the battery.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the bulletin on memory seat module battery drain.

issues.t: Oil leak from the engine bedplate
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine and oil residue on the lower engine.
issues.why: GM found a bolt in the engine bedplate (the lower block casting) can leak oil and released a sealing procedure.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the leak source confirmed before larger repairs are done.

issues.t: Oil or coolant leak with the check engine light on
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the engine may misfire, and oil or coolant may show up in a spark plug well.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for oil or coolant leaking into the spark plug tubes or out of the engine, with the light on.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level. If coolant is dropping, stop driving and have it diagnosed before the engine is damaged.

issues.t: Water on the front floor or musty smell
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front floor on either side, or a mildew smell inside.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for water reaching the front floor, often from the A/C drain or a body seal.
issues.next: Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and have the leak found.

issues.t: Steering Assist Is Reduced message
issues.sym: A warning that steering assist is reduced, and the steering feels heavy.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this message with steering module communication codes.
issues.next: Drive slowly and allow extra effort to steer. Have the steering system diagnosed before driving normally.

issues.t: Cracked catalytic converter rattle or exhaust smell
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from under the car, or an exhaust smell inside the cabin.
issues.why: GM found catalytic converters that can crack.
issues.next: Do not ignore exhaust smell in the cabin; drive with windows open and get it checked soon.

issues.t: Rear clunk over bumps from loose shock bolts
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear when driving over bumps.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin to re-tighten the rear shock bolts to stop this clunk.
issues.next: Have the rear shock mounting bolts checked and torqued.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for warm A/C output, including bent expansion valve tubes on some replacement evaporators.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures checked and any bulletin applied before adding refrigerant.

issues.t: Keyless entry and push-button start not working
issues.sym: The doors will not unlock by touch or the car will not start with one or both key fobs.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for passive entry and passive start not working with one or both fobs.
issues.next: Try the backup start procedure in the owner manual. Have a dealer check the bulletin and the fobs.

issues.t: Radio audio or warning chimes cut out
issues.sym: The audio drops out, or warning chimes do not sound.
issues.why: GM ran a customer satisfaction program on some 2018 Cadillac sedans for lost infotainment audio and chimes.
issues.next: Ask a Cadillac dealer whether the program was done on your car. Missing chimes means you may miss warnings.

issues.t: Engine stops after long idle in Park
issues.sym: The engine shuts off on its own after idling in Park for a long time.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for engines stopping after extended idle in Park.
issues.next: Avoid long idles until it is checked. Ask a dealer about the bulletin and any software update.

issues.t: Engine knock or rattle
issues.sym: A knocking, rattling or squealing noise from the engine.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin on how to inspect an engine with this noise and decide if it needs replacement.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away. If the knock is loud or the oil light flickers, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Headlight or taillight condensation
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlights or taillights.
issues.why: GM has guidelines for when lamp condensation is normal and when a leaking lamp should be replaced.
issues.next: Light fog that clears is normal. Standing water inside needs a new lamp.

issues.t: Brake booster pump connector can melt (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, smoke from the engine bay, or a brake warning message.
issues.why: Corrosion in the relay connector for the brake booster pump can cause a short that melts the connector and creates a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke, stop and shut the car off. Ask a dealer to check this recall.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake can stay partly applied (recall)
issues.sym: A hot brake smell, smoke from a rear wheel, or the car feeling like it is dragging.
issues.why: The rear brake pads can stay partly pressed on the rotors after the electronic parking brake releases, building heat that could start a fire.
issues.next: If a rear wheel smells hot or smokes, pull over and let it cool. Have a dealer check the parking brake recall.

issues.t: Brake lights can flash when not braking (recall)
issues.sym: Other drivers say your brake lights flash even when you are not slowing down.
issues.why: A fault can make the brake lamps flash when the car is not braking, which can confuse drivers behind you.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the brake lamp recall.

issues.t: Front head restraint may not stay in position (recall)
issues.sym: A head restraint that is lower than it should be or does not lock in place.
issues.why: Some head restraints may sit too low, which raises the risk of neck injury in a crash.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the head restraint recall.

issues.t: Steering parts may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the steering, loose or wandering steering, or loss of steering.
issues.why: On a small number of cars, steering fasteners were not tightened correctly and could separate.
issues.next: If the steering feels loose, stop driving and have it towed. Ask a dealer whether your car is included.

issues.t: Side airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs; the risk is during a crash.
issues.why: On a small number of cars, a side airbag inflator could rupture in a crash and throw metal pieces.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for this recall right away.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons may lack coating (recall)
issues.sym: Reduced braking power or a brake pedal that feels different over time.
issues.why: Rear caliper pistons may not have enough protective coating, which can lead to corrosion and weaker braking.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the rear caliper recall on your VIN.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle can separate in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No sign while driving; the buckle could detach in a crash.
issues.why: On a small number of cars, a rivet that holds the buckle to its mounting strap may be missing.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for this recall.
